v11.74 - x-120 ve x-122: model+effort çifti öldüğü yerde değil, söz verildiği yerde reddediliyor

A mission row moved between engines keeps its model, and a model changed under a
kept effort keeps that effort. The composer's narrow strip noticed both and
asked; `Keep as they are` promised, in its own tooltip, that the draft's refusal
list above Start would say so. The list never looked: `previewMission` asked
`engineRefusal` (can this machine run that engine at all) and
`headlessEffortRefusal` (does that engine have an effort flag) and nothing else.
Whether the resolved engine's catalogue HAS that model, and whether that model
takes that effort, was checked by no door on the mission path — so a Codex model
kept on a Claude row, or `medium` left behind by a model that offers low/high,
reached a real `--model`/`--effort` and was answered by the CLI hours later in an
archive file nobody is reading.

The planner had the same hole one control over (X-122): `plannerModel` was
checked for legal characters and `plannerEffort` against the shared effort
vocabulary — legal words, illegal combination — and then went onto every
planning call of the run.

`capabilityRefusal` (core/models.ts) is the one gate now, beside `narrowLaunch`
rather than inside it: narrowing is right for a picker the user is still moving,
and wrong for a launch that has already been asked for. It is asked for every
worker on the engine that row really lands on, and for the planner on Claude
Code's own catalogue. It names what the engine does offer and what the model does
take, so a fault is fixable in one pass instead of one attempt at a time.

What it will NOT do, deliberately:
- refuse from an alias guess — only `source: 'catalog'` (the engine's own answer)
  may refuse a model; a `settings` list and an absent catalogue refuse nothing;
- answer a question that already has an owner — an engine with no effort flag at
  all is `headlessEffortRefusal`'s, and two refusals for one fault is how two
  wordings start disagreeing;
- treat an alias as a stranger — `opus` and the dated id the CLI records are one
  model, matched on the same family+variant key the catalogue merge dedupes on.

Because X-119 landed first, this reaches the Start button and `missions.start`
as well as the preview, in the same sentence: a draft carrying an off-catalogue
pair cannot create a spec, a run or a task.

Measured in test/test_models.js (13 new): off-catalogue model, model-specific
effort vocabulary, the Default box judged by the shared list, an empty
vocabulary, settings-source and absent catalogues refusing nothing, the
no-effort engine left alone, alias/dated-id/1m-variant matching, and a real typo
still refused. test/test_bridge.js pins the wiring for the worker rows and the
planner, and the op's describe.
